fieldDescription: How much the Remnant network's grudge (and the colony crisis bar) grows for each Remnant hull your fleet destroys.
Threat points for each Remnant frigate destroyed.
Threat points for each Remnant destroyer destroyed.
Threat points for each Remnant cruiser destroyed.
Threat points for each Remnant capital destroyed.
Threat points for destroying a Remnant Nexus (the station). Intended to be the single biggest contributor.
Multiplies all kill point values. Raise for faster testing, lower for a slower burn.
How the accumulated grudge translates into ongoing pressure between retaliation strikes.
Higher = slower monthly bar creep. Monthly progress = 1 + grudge / this value, capped below.
Cap on how many crisis-bar points the standing grudge adds per month.
Hunter-killer fleets stay away until the grudge reaches this. Below it you only see the monthly bar creep.
Grudge at which hunter-killer fleet presence in your systems reaches its cap.
Cap on hostile fleet presence magnitude per system (vanilla crises use ~0.5).
Maximum simultaneous Remnant hunter-killer groups per player system.
How destroying Remnant Nexus stations weakens the network - and whether the threat can be ended permanently.

If on: destroying every Remnant Nexus in the sector triggers one final convergence strike - defeat it and the crisis ends permanently. If off: the classic eternal grudge - dormant forces strike forever.

Minimum pressure multiplier as the network fragments. Monthly progress, hunter presence, and strike strength scale from full (all Nexuses alive) down to this (nearly all destroyed). Only applies when permanent neutralization is on.
The final convergence strike's strength as a multiple of the normal strike cap. The network's last gasp should be its biggest.
The network's warning shot: a recon force probing your defenses, fired from the crisis bar's minor event stage. Happens at most once per campaign (vanilla minor-event rule).
The reconnaissance cannot be rolled until the grudge reaches this. Keep it well below the strike threshold so the probe arrives first.
Combined fleet strength of the recon force (the full strike defaults to 50 base). Scaled down as the network fragments.
The crisis payload: a Remnant force that attempts to saturation-bombard one of your colonies.
The retaliation strike cannot be rolled until the grudge reaches this. (~1 Nexus by default.)
Base combined fleet strength of the strike force (vanilla Remnant attack uses ~50).
Additional strike strength per point of grudge.
Hard cap on strike force strength before the per-defeat escalation multiplier.
Each defeated strike makes the next this much stronger (0.25 means 25 percent stronger).
Fraction of grudge remaining after you defeat a strike (0.5 = halved).
Back-tracing active hunter-killers to the command Nexuses that dispatch them - map markers you can hunt down, pirate-base style.

While hunter-killers are active, your polity periodically traces a surviving Remnant Nexus and marks its system on the map as an intel entry. Entering a system with a live Nexus reveals it immediately.
Days of active hunter-killer presence between each new Nexus location being revealed (nearest to your colonies first).
Destroyed Nexus stations yield fragments of their Domain-era gate control cores - each one repairs a single dormant Gate, without the Academy questline (but no free sector-wide unlock either).

Destroying a Remnant Nexus adds a Gate Control Fragment to the battle salvage. Take it to any dormant Gate and choose 'Repair the Gate' - only that Gate comes online. The first repair also yields a working Janus Device (required to actually transit).
The last Remnant Nexus guards a Domain-era planetkiller: destroying it adds the weapon to the battle salvage (once per campaign; skipped if the vanilla questline already produced it).
While you hold the planetkiller, an intel entry offers surrendering it to the Luddic Path for the permanent vanilla pather agreement - holy peace, cells stand down for good.
Tools for testing the mod. Debug actions run once when a game is loaded.
Logs grudge changes, kill tallies, and crisis rolls to starsector.log (prefix [RemRet]).
If you own no colony when a game loads, transfers the nearest small NPC market to you so the crisis system activates. Turn off again after testing.
On load, if this is above 0 and your grudge is 0, sets your grudge to this value (once per game). Feeds monthly progress; does not set the bar directly.
On load, if you already own a colony, pushes the crisis bar to 600 so the Remnant retaliation strike fires immediately. Turn off again afterward.
